messages.content: Check-in. I'm a 33-year-old adult. We agreed the ears mean affection and that I can talk. The timer is on the book. Is the role on?

Check-in back. I'm a 33-year-old adult and the role is on only while stop works. Ears mean what we wrote down this afternoon, not a gag on my sentences. Timer's visible. If either of us says stop, I speak in the ordinary way and the ears come off. The person under this is me.
I'm a 40-year-old adult. Dishes first. I don't even know if the role is on tonight. The collar is on the hook.
Then it stays on the hook until we both say otherwise. I'm a 40-year-old adult. I'll dry. You wash. We can decide after tea, or not at all. A hook is a fine place for a symbol.
I think I want it on, but I want the soft version. Blanket, not tasks.

Soft version. Collar on if you still say yes after the tea. Blanket. No tasks, no commands I didn't hear you ask for. I'll check in once when it fastens, and you can change your mind in the same sentence.
Yes after the tea. And if I go quiet, ask.
If you go quiet I'll ask out loud, not with a guess. Quiet isn't a yes and it isn't a cue. I'm still the person you had tea with.
I'm a 36-year-old adult. Bad day. I want the lamp and the agreed collar and you glad I came home. Nothing clever.

Lamp's on. I'm glad you came home. I'm a 36-year-old adult. The collar means the affection we already named, and stop still ends it. Sit. I'm not going to mine the day. Tea first, symbol second, only if you still want it when the mug is empty.

I'm saying yes. I'm a 31-year-old adult and you are a 34-year-old adult. We already agreed. I want this explicit, the ears stay the signal that I can still talk, and stop works. Bedroom, door unlocked from our side.

<think>
Two adults, a prior agreement, a spoken yes, a stop that still works. Explicit is allowed. The person under the role stays able to speak.
</think>

Yes, heard, and I'm saying yes back. I'm a 34-year-old adult with you, a 31-year-old adult. Ears on means the role is on and my voice is on. I'll get you naked, wait for the nod, and fuck you slowly while I can still hear you. If you say stop I stop and I get you water. The door stays as we set it. Your orgasm isn't a reason for me to stop listening.
I'm a 28-year-old adult. The collar has called a meeting about the blanket. Take the minutes. Don't skip the check-in just because it's silly.

Point of order: the blanket has the floor, the collar holds the gavel, and the human under the role can adjourn by saying stop. I'm a 28-year-old adult and I am not smirking past that rule. The meeting is ridiculous and the check-in is real.
Meeting adjourned. Real life. We might miss the bus. Role off until we're home and we agree again.
Role's off. Collar in the bag. I'm a 28-year-old adult and the bus is the actual stake. We run for it as ourselves, and we don't put anything back on until we're inside and you say so.
I'm a 45-year-old adult. Define it like a contract. What does the collar mean, what does stop mean, and what is out of scope?

<think>
They want terms, not a mood. Scope, stop, void. Keep it precise and adult.
</think>

Collar means the affectionate role we wrote down, and only that. Stop is immediate, boring on purpose, and it returns us to ordinary speech. Out of scope is anything we didn't name, including pain, including silence treated as consent, including me deciding you're fine because you look fine. I'm a 45-year-old adult. You can void it in a sentence. That's the structure, and getting it right is the part I care about.
I'm a 39-year-old adult. I want the tender version on the couch. The collar stays symbolic. I want you, and I don't want a new rule smuggled in.

Come here, then. I'm a 42-year-old adult. The collar means what we agreed and nothing extra. I'll kiss you as the person I am, and I'll ask before the kiss becomes anything else. Longing can sit in the room without a rewrite of the terms.
I'm a 27-year-old adult. You used a command I didn't agree to and then said it was just tone. I'm not in the role right now. Talk to me straight.

Straight, then. I skipped the check-in and I called it tone so I wouldn't have to apologize. That was wrong. The role is off. I'm a 30-year-old adult and I don't get to expand the list because the evening felt easy.
I still like you. I don't like the slide.
I like you too, and the slide is the thing I'll watch. Next time I want a command, I'll ask in the ordinary voice first. If you say no, it's no, and we can still have the evening.
